title: Vectors: Column Vectors, Magnitude and Position Vectors
seo_title: Sec 4 Vectors Worksheets: Free Secondary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: use of vector notation; representing a vector as a directed line segment; translation by a vector; position vectors; magnitude of a vector as √(x² + y²); sum and difference of two vectors; multiplication of a vector by a scalar
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 maths worksheets on vectors in two dimensions: column vectors, magnitude, adding and subtracting vectors, scalar multiples, position vectors, translations and parallel vectors. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A column vector shows the move across (top) and up or down (bottom).
key_sub: Magnitude = √(x² + y²); AB = OB − OA; parallel vectors are scalar multiples.
body_html:
How it works

  • A column vector gives the move across (top number: + right, − left) and the move up or down (bottom number: + up, − down).
  • The magnitude of a vector with components x and y is √(x² + y²).
  • Add, subtract and multiply by a scalar component by component.
  • For position vectors, AB = OB − OA (end minus start).
  • Two vectors are parallel if one is a scalar multiple of the other.
Example

A is (1, 2) and B is (4, −2). Find AB and |AB|.

AB = (4 − 1, −2 − 2) = (3, −4)

|AB| = √(9 + 16)

Answer: (3, −4) and 5

Example

Find k if (2, k) is parallel to (6, 9).

(6, 9) = 3 × (2, 3)

Answer: k = 3

Common mistakes

  • Writing the vertical move on top. The horizontal move goes on top.
  • Forgetting the minus sign for a move left or down.
  • Working out OA − OB for AB. It is OB − OA.
  • Adding the components for the magnitude instead of using √(x² + y²).

faq.a: Two numbers written one above the other: the top number is the horizontal move and the bottom number is the vertical move.

faq.q: How do you find the magnitude of a vector?
faq.a: Use Pythagoras' theorem: √(x² + y²), where x and y are the components.

faq.q: How do you find AB from position vectors?
faq.a: Subtract the start from the end: AB = OB − OA.

faq.q: How do you know two vectors are parallel?
faq.a: One is a number times the other. For example (4, 6) = 2 × (2, 3), so they are parallel.

items.q: 1−2 is parallel to 4k. Find k.

items.q: Given that x + 6y − 2 = 55, find x and y.
items.e: Equal vectors have equal components: x + 6 = 5 gives x = −1, and y − 2 = 5 gives y = 7. x = −1, y = 7.
